High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Indore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Shri Ashish Gupta - Advocate for the appellant.
Shri Rahul Solanki - Govt. Advocate for the respondent/
Heard on I.A No.3833/2025 which is an application for suspension of sentence under Section 389(1) of the Cr.P.C., 1973 filed on behalf of the appellant- Chandan.

2. The appellant has been convicted under Section 343 of the IPC and sentenced to undergo 01 year R.I with fine of Rs.500/- and Section 366 of the IPC and sentenced to undergo 03 years R.I with fine of Rs.500/- and Section 376(2)(n) r/w 109 of the IPC and sentenced to undergo 10 years R.I with fine of Rs.1,000/- alongwith default stipulations respectively vide judgment dated 24.01.2024 passed in SC No.600013/2016 by Special Judge, POCSO Act, 2012 Badwani (M.P).
3.
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that appellant has falsely been implicated in the case.
The appeal is of the year 2024 and final conclusion of trial will take considerable long time for its hearing.

Hence, he prays for suspension of jail sentence.
4.
Learned counsel for the respondent/State has opposed the prayer and prayed for its rejection.
5. Considering the para 23 of the judgment, without commenting on 2 CRA-2319-2024 the merits of the case, we are inclined to suspend the remaining jail sentence of the appellant.

6. Accordingly, I.A. No.3833/2025, is allowed and it is directed that upon depositing fine amount if already not deposited and on furnishing a personal bond by the appellant in the sum of Rs.50,000/-
(Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with a solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the learned trial Court for his regular appearance before the Registry of this Court on 03/11/2025 and on all other subsequent dates, as may be fixed by the Registry in this behalf, the execution of the custodial part of the sentence imposed on the appellant shall remain suspended, till the final disposal of this appeal.
7. I.A. No.3833/2025 stands allowed and disposed off.
List the matter for final hearing in due course.
